title: Sequencing & Handoff Charter for Cross-Functional Release Windows
creator: Maya Gonzalez
description: Goal: create an operational charter and lightweight toolset to sequence and hand off interdependent work across Eng / Design / Security / Infra for quarterly release windows. Motivation: recent rollouts revealed missed sequencing (KV cache resets, UX contract drift, and late security signoffs) that increased rollback risk and on-call load. This ticket will produce: 1) a sequencing rubric to classify blockers vs soft-dependencies, 2) a single source-of-truth CSV/board for each release window, 3) a gating checklist for go/no-go, and 4) an escalation and backstop playbook for last-mile unblocks.
acceptance_criteria: Sequencing rubric published to Confluence and approved by Eng, Design, Security, Infra leads
Release Window CSV template created and consumed by at least two active projects for the upcoming cycle
Gating checklist implemented as a lightweight workflow in release board and covered in runbook
At least one cross-functional tabletop exercised with a simulated late-signoff and documented runbook updates
Stakeholder alignment session recorded and distributed with clear owners for each critical-path item
notes: Why sequencing matters: runtime changes (kernel selection, KV cache semantics) require deterministic staging order to avoid KV eviction or warm/cold regressions
Prefer a simple CSV/board-first approach before investing in automation — low friction adoption is priority
Tie gating checklist items to dashboards (error rate, 95th latency, deploy frequency) so decisions are signal-driven
